full_text:
Waste management has become a major challenge in modern cities due to rapid urbanization and increasing population. Traditional waste collection systems often lead to overflowing bins, environmental pollution, and inefficient use of resources. To address this issue, this project proposes a Smart Waste Management System using Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning techniques.

The system uses IoT sensors placed inside waste bins to monitor the waste level in real time. When the bin reaches a certain threshold, the sensor sends data to a cloud server. The collected data is analyzed using machine learning algorithms to predict waste generation patterns and optimize waste collection routes.

This interdisciplinary approach integrates computer science for data processing, electronics for sensor-based monitoring, and environmental science for sustainable waste management. The proposed system helps municipalities reduce operational costs, improve waste collection efficiency, and maintain cleaner urban environments.

suggestions.description: Design and execute a pilot study in a selected urban environment to gather empirical data, validate the system's real-world performance in terms of waste level accuracy, prediction efficacy, route optimization, and measure tangible impacts on operational costs and environmental benefits.

suggestions.description: Investigate optimal sensor placement strategies, sensor types, and communication protocols to ensure robust data collection, energy efficiency, and scalability of the IoT network across diverse urban topographies and waste bin distributions.

In the last few years, journals and
conferences have started receiving a very
large number of research paper submissions.
Because of this, editors often face problems
while manually arranging papers under the
correct technical domains. Choosing the
right domain is important for reviewer
selection,
organizing
publications,
and
keeping proper records. When submissions
increase, manual classification takes more
time and mainly depends on the editor’s
individual knowledge and experience.
In order to overcome this difficulty, this
paper proposes SmartDocAI, a research
paper
domain
classification
system
developed to support editors during the
submission stage. The system studies the
abstract of a paper and the keywords given
by the authors to decide the most suitable
research area. It makes use of basic natural
language processing techniques to clean and
analyze the text. A transformer-based
learning model is then applied to understand
the overall meaning of the content. Using
this approach, the system is able to classify
papers into domains such as Artificial
Intelligence,
Data
Science,
Machine
Learning,
Cyber
Security,
Internet of
Things, and Cloud Computing.
Along with domain prediction, the system
also generates a confidence score for each
result. This score helps editors decide
whether the classification can be accepted
directly or needs manual checking. Separate
user interfaces are available for authors,
editors,
and
administrators
so
that
submission handling and verification can be
carried out smoothly. During testing, the
system showed stable performance and
reduced the amount of effort required for
manual
domain
classification.
Overall,
SmartDocAI helps editors manage large
numbers of research submissions in a more
organized and efficient way.

These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive edge resource management to enhance the scalability and responsiveness of IoT applications.

full_text:
In the last few years, journals and 
conferences have started receiving a very 
large number of research paper submissions. 
Because of this, editors often face problems 
while manually arranging papers under the 
correct technical domains. Choosing the 
right domain is important for reviewer 
selection, 
organizing 
publications, 
and 
keeping proper records. When submissions 
increase, manual classification takes more 
time and mainly depends on the editor’s 
individual knowledge and experience. 
 
In order to overcome this difficulty, this 
paper proposes SmartDocAI, a research 
paper 
domain 
classification 
system 
developed to support editors during the 
submission stage. The system studies the 
abstract of a paper and the keywords given 
by the authors to decide the most suitable 
research area. It makes use of basic natural 
language processing techniques to clean and 
analyze the text. A transformer-based 
learning model is then applied to understand 
the overall meaning of the content. Using 
this approach, the system is able to classify 
papers into domains such as Artificial 
Intelligence, 
Data 
Science, 
Machine 
Learning, 
Cyber 
Security, 
Internet of 
Things, and Cloud Computing. 
 
Along with domain prediction, the system 
also generates a confidence score for each 
result. This score helps editors decide 
whether the classification can be accepted 
directly or needs manual checking. Separate 
user interfaces are available for authors, 
editors, 
and 
administrators 
so 
that 
submission handling and verification can be 
carried out smoothly. During testing, the 
system showed stable performance and 
reduced the amount of effort required for 
manual 
domain 
classification. 
Overall, 
SmartDocAI helps editors manage large 
numbers of research submissions in a more 
organized and efficient way.

text_preview: This paper presents a novel deep learning architecture for real-time object detection in constrained...
full_text: This paper presents a novel deep learning architecture for real-time object detection in constrained environments. We utilize a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) combined with an optimized attention mechanism to achieve high precision with low computational overhead. Our model, evaluated on the COCO dataset, demonstrates a 15% improvement in inference speed compared to state-of-the-art methods while maintaining comparable mean Average Precision (mAP). The proposed system is particularly suitable for deployment on edge devices with limited memory and processing power.

text_preview: SmartDocAI is an intelligent research paper classification system designed to automate the organizat...
full_text: SmartDocAI is an intelligent research paper classification system designed to automate the organization and management of scientific publications using Large Language Models (LLMs). In traditional academic publishing workflows, research paper categorization is largely performed manually by editors and reviewers, making the process time-consuming, expertise-dependent, and prone to inconsistency and human bias. With the rapid growth of scientific literature, manual classification has become inefficient and difficult to scale. To address this challenge, SmartDocAI employs advanced natural language processing and LLM-based semantic analysis to automatically classify research papers into appropriate technical domains such as Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cyber Security, Internet of Things, and Cloud Computing. The system provides two dedicated interfaces: an Author/Editor interface for secure paper or abstract submission and an Administrator interface featuring a centralized dashboard with modules for domain prediction, confidence analysis, paper history, and editorial review. Using a fine-tuned transformer-based language model, SmartDocAI analyzes scientific text, extracts semantic features, and generates accurate domain predictions with confidence scores. All classification results are systematically stored for auditing, retrieval, and trend analysis. The system significantly improves editorial workflow efficiency, reduces manual workload, and enables faster, more reliable paper routing and indexing, offering a scalable solution for modern academic publishing environments.

full_text: We propose a novel attention-based neural network architecture for natural language processing tasks. By leveraging multi-head attention mechanisms and positional encodings, the model achieves state-of-the-art performance on machine translation and sentiment analysis benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that this architecture significantly reduces training time while maintaining high accuracy compared to recurrent neural networks. Furthermore, we introduce a new regularization technique to prevent overfitting in large-scale language models, ensuring robust generalization across diverse datasets.
